title: Content `annotations`
description: The `audience`, `priority` and `lastModified` hints that content blocks, resources and prompt messages may carry.
question: Do content annotations survive to the agent?
notes: Content annotations reach neither adapter that gets to 2026-07-28; 3 cannot reach the revision.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI 1.15.1 requires MCP Python SDK 1.26.x, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 requires mcp<2.0.0, so it cannot open a 2026-07-28 adapter session.
notes_by_num.3: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0: the `audience` and `priority` annotations on a content block are not carried onto the output item.
notes_by_num.4: Pydantic AI 2.40.0: content is returned as plain strings and binary objects, neither of which has a slot for annotations.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra 1.17.3 negotiated MCP 2025-11-25. The scanner refused to compare that capture with a 2026-07-28 source.

verdict.headline: Destroyed by both adapters that reach 2026-07-28.
verdict.detail: `audience` and `priority` are the server's only way to say who a piece of content is for and how much it matters. Both adapters discard them, so a UI built on either cannot honour the distinction. CrewAI, LangChain and Mastra cannot negotiate MCP 2026-07-28, so they reach none of it.

usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
why: Annotations are how a server says who a piece of content is for and how much it matters. A client that drops them cannot filter assistant-only content out of a user view, cannot prioritise what to keep when context runs short, and cannot sort by recency.
